data.note:
Reflection note:

Conclusion **Protein degradation** confirmed correct after unblinding to proteasome inhibitor I (PubChem CID 16760625, BBBC021 annotated as Protein degradation; ChEMBL no curated mechanism - lookup e16).

Blinded evidence supported this: NSC vote 3/4 wells Protein degradation (e8) with similarities 0.637-0.711 to reference proteasome inhibitors, consistent elongated nuclei/large area/low DNA mean and preserved actin vs DMSO (e2-e4,e6). High dose (10 µM) discordance to Microtubule stabilizers with extreme tub_glcm_contrast z=30.4 (e7,e9) was interpreted as off-target tubulin bundling, with no mitotic elevation (e11) to support true microtubule/Aurora/Eg5 MoA.

Literature check: site-specific proteasome inhibitors reviewed (PMID:35053202) and MG132 proteasome inhibitor effects on cells (PMID:22897979, PMID:41631982) align with observed proteotoxic stress phenotype.

reflection.text:
After unblinding to proteasome inhibitor I (PubChem CID 16760625) the verdict was correct: truth Protein degradation vs agent Protein degradation p=0.62. This was not overconfident and that calibration was appropriate given the evidence.

What we got right:
- Early sampling strategy worked. Acquiring dose 5 (1 uM, e2) and dose 6 (3 uM, e3) first captured the core phenotype: very high nuc_eccentricity (z=+11.8 at 1 uM, +10.5 at 3 uM), consistently low nuc_dna_mean (z=-7.6 and -7.2), and increased nuclear area/integrated DNA. Acquiring dose 3 (0.1 uM, e6) then showed onset at low dose with same triad: nuc_eccentricity z=+8.7, nuc_dna_mean z=-7.1, nuc_area z=+5.9. That persistence across 0.1-3 uM argued for a single dose-responsive MoA rather than noisy well effects.
- We correctly used the comparison tools. describe_phenotype e4 was uninformative (density lower vs DMSO, 8 observations, candidates: unknown) and we did not over-weight it. compare_to_reference_atlas e5 and e8 gave conflicting signals: NSC voted Protein degradation 2/2 then 3/4, while k-neighbour plurality was DNA replication 4/10 and DNA damage 3/10 with Protein degradation only 2/10. We put weight on NSC, which was the right discriminator here; kNN overlap reflects known phenotypic similarity between proteasome inhibition (large, flat, elongated cells/nuclei with altered DNA staining) and replication stress.
- Dose-response checks were decisive for ruling out mitosis-linked MoAs. frac_mitotic_like e11 rho=-0.77 p=0.23 did not increase with dose, which contradicts Aurora, Eg5, and microtubule destabilizers that typically elevate mitotic fraction. We kept those at 0.01-0.02 in hypothesis_history step 13. cell_count e12 rho=-1.00 p=0 and tub_glcm_contrast e9 rho=+1.00 p=0 both showed clean monotonic trends, supporting cytotoxicity with cytoskeletal texture change but not diagnostic alone.

What misled us or what we missed:
- The high dose well w_d128269dd7 e7 at 10 uM was highly discordant: tub_glcm_contrast z=+30.4, tub_mean z=+11.3, tub_std z=+9.7. That extreme tubulin texture/bundling phenotype is why Microtubule stabilizers was retained at p=0.18 and listed as contradicting e7 for the Protein degradation hypothesis. We correctly flagged it as "1 discordant high dose" in the submit rationale, but we did not have data to resolve whether this is secondary proteasome-inhibition induced aggresome/tubulin remodeling vs a true high-dose off-target stabilizer effect.
- We did not acquire any replicate 2 wells and only sampled 4/8 doses (0.1, 1, 3, 10 uM), all rep 1. Without a second replicate at dose 7 we could not test reproducibility of the z=+30.4 texture spike. Dose-response of nuc_eccentricity e10 rho=-0.40 p=0.6 also showed no positive trend, indicating a plateau/desaturation rather than linear dose response, which we did not follow up.
- Literature search in this run did not resolve the ambiguity. search_literature e17 for 'proteasome inhibitor proteasome degradation MG132' returned 3606 hits with 5 returned including general MG132 reviews PMID 41631982, PMID 35053202, PMID 24702728, PMID 21843349, PMID 22897979, but none specifically describing the elongated nucleus/low DNA mean or tubulin bundling phenotype. The second search e18 for 'proteasome inhibition tubulin microtubule morphology cell elongation' returned 0 hits. So we had no literature anchor for the morphology and made the claim without citation, which is appropriate.
- lookup_compound e15/e16 correctly showed no curated mechanisms in ChEMBL and name/BBBC021 structure agreement, so we could not leverage external annotation and had to rely entirely on image profile matching.

Why and lesson: The nuclear elongation + decondensed/low-intensity DNA phenotype across multiple doses plus NSC 3/4 consensus outweighed the single-well tubulin extreme. The next experiment we proposed - ubiquitin IF/Proteasome-Glo vs reference proteasome inhibitor and microtubule stabilizer at 0.1-3 uM - remains the right way to test primary vs secondary tubulin effect. For future runs, acquire a replicate 2 at the high dose and an intermediate dose (e.g., 0.3 uM) to confirm texture outlier reproducibility and plateau behavior before closing.

No clinical implications are discussed; this is in vitro screening data only.

## Reflection
